kinds.d: Disposable or cloth garment worn by a baby to absorb urine and faeces.
Padded, wipe-clean mat for changing a baby's nappy.
Small tub made for bathing a baby.
Small free-standing toilet bowl for a young child.
Child-sized seat that fits on an adult toilet.
Teat for a baby to suck that is not used for feeding.
Ring, key or toy of silicone, rubber or wood for a baby to chew to soothe teething gums.

notes: All seven old kinds kept one-to-one (k99–k105); nothing merged or dropped. 'Pacifier' renamed to the British 'Dummy', with pacifier and soother as aliases. Nappy given types disposable, cloth, swim nappy and pull-up. Teether given types ring, key and toy, taken from its old definition. Definitions tightened and every old source kept. All kinds tagged baby. The old data had no models or ranges, so none were added. The suggested market brands (Pampers, Huggies, MAM, Philips Avent, Sophie la Girafe) were left out because the brief allows them only if already in the data and this shelf is restraint-only with no new research.
